headline: The House voted down H.R. 1 in December 2017, so this 2017 tax overhaul and Arctic drilling bill never became law; this explains what it would have done.
what_it_does: If adopted, the bill would have lowered individual income tax brackets, nearly doubled the standard deduction, and raised the child tax credit to $2,000 per child. It would have cut the corporate tax rate to a flat 21 percent, repealed the corporate alternative minimum tax, and moved toward a territorial system for foreign profits. It would also have opened the Coastal Plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge in Alaska to a federal oil and gas leasing program.

who_it_affects.how: They would have received a larger child tax credit and a higher standard deduction, but would have lost personal exemptions and several itemized deductions.
New mortgages would have been limited to $750,000 for the interest deduction, and home equity loan interest would have stopped being deductible.

who_it_affects.group: State and local taxpayers who itemize
who_it_affects.how: Deductions for state and local taxes would have been capped at $10,000 per year.

who_it_affects.group: Owners of pass-through businesses such as sole proprietorships and partnerships
who_it_affects.how: They would have been able to deduct 20 percent of qualified business income, subject to income limits for certain service businesses.
Their federal tax rate would have dropped to a flat 21 percent, and the corporate alternative minimum tax would have been repealed.

who_it_affects.group: People who buy health insurance on their own
who_it_affects.how: The federal penalty for going without minimum essential health coverage would have been repealed.

who_it_affects.group: Students and families saving for education
who_it_affects.how: 529 plan funds could have been used for K-12 private, public, or religious school tuition.
The estate and gift tax exemption would have doubled from $5 million to $10 million.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of the Coastal Plain of Alaska and oil and gas companies
who_it_affects.how: Interior would have been required to hold at least two lease sales within 10 years covering at least 400,000 acres each.
